title: Finishing a typed title on a video never stalls the app
goal: When you type a title over a video and press Command Return to finish it, the app freezes for about a fifth of a second while it lays out the new Title track. Picking a transition tile at a cut also holds for about 80 ms. Both should answer inside the 50 ms the video goals promise, so finishing a title and picking a dissolve feel instant.
notes: Reproduced by the manager on 2026-10-16 at HEAD cac7a368 with Scripts/playtest-all.sh --no-build an-editing-session-walk, twice. Run 1: step 53 'key command+return taken by responder chain', step 54 'wait 1.0s asked, quiet after 0.97s; mainBusy 877.0ms over 299 passes, longest 197.4ms from 458ms in'. Run 2: step 54 'never went quiet (13 of 16 slices busy, busiest 367.4ms); mainBusy 869.2ms over 291 passes, longest 202.7ms from 422ms in'. Step 40 press 'Cross dissolve' in At this cut: longest 67.8 ms (run 1), 82.5 ms (run 2). Logs at /tmp/photonz-playtest/an-editing-session-walk/log.json. The hold starts ~0.4 s after the commit, so suspect the deferred work after a text commit on a video: the new Title track being made (411c247d puts a title on a track named Title), the timeline rows re-laying out, the panel rebuilding for the new pick, or the title's text being rasterised for the first frame. Profile before guessing. The cut click, first animated value pick and its undo stay with clicking-a-cut-keying-a-value-and-undoing-it-ans (blocked on its card; its notes hold the panel-teardown attribution, which may explain the tile pick too). Needs a perf note in the commit if it touches the composite path.
acceptance: The stall after Command Return on a typed title in an-editing-session-walk is found and its causes fixed: the longest pass drops from about 200 ms to under 100 ms in three runs in a row
Picking Cross dissolve from the At this cut tiles holds under 65 ms in three runs in a row (was 68-82 ms)

The walk's timing claims fail a slide back to the old stalls (100 ms after Command Return, 65 ms on the tile), and the remaining stretch to 50 ms is its own task (finishing-a-typed-title-and-picking-a-dissolve-l)

Try path, no flag changed from Next defaults: open the sample recording, press T, click the picture, type a title, press Command Return; the playhead and the panel answer without the old fifth-of-a-second hold
Audit written under queue/audits/ with before and after numbers; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: acceptance rewritten to the slice that shipped: the original 50 ms items moved verbatim to finishing-a-typed-title-and-picking-a-dissolve-l (see the scope line above)

reproduced at HEAD 03790d16: wait after Command Return longest 189.0 ms (423 ms in); Cross dissolve tile 72.6 ms. Profiled with xctrace Time Profiler attached to the probe plus temporary pass/arrival logs (removed before commit).

cause 1 (190 ms + 150 ms): the title's Effects section (two shadows, 528 pt) arrives last in the one-per-pass chain, 92 pt under the fold so inside PanelBodyReach's 120 pt reach; it measured whole, the height budget then gave it a 252 pt ceiling, and SectionBodyHost moved the body into a ScrollView, which changed its identity, so every control was torn down and built again in the same pass. Fix: a section the dock may shorten (DockMetrics.scrollingSections) always sits in its scroller, sized to its content via fixedSize while whole and scrollDisabled; only the height follows the ceiling (InspectorSections.swift SectionBodyHost). Verified a real wheel over a whole Effects body still scrolls the dock (temporary walk, before/after pictures).

cause 2: building both shadow panes in one pass (~93 ms) plus SwiftUI's AccessibilityNode.updateFocus walk over the new controls. Fix: effect panes arrive one per pass (PanelRowsArrival after index+1, new waitsForReach:false because the nearest scroller is now the Effects list itself, not the dock).

cause 3: ~30 ms of the commit pass was AppKit filling every menu (Services, Window, SwiftUI) to look for a Command Return key equivalent nobody has. InlineTextView now answers Command Return (command alone) in performKeyEquivalent while it is first responder. Walk line now reads 'taken by window'.

measurement: the key step did not honour setup.timedWithoutMarkers, and the guarded wait after a timed step put the ~800 probe marker views back up half way through the work it guarded. Key steps now take markers down; a wait with longestUnderMS (PlaytestStep.guardsTheStepBefore, unit tested) keeps them down until it has read. With markers up the same commit read 70-80 ms passes that were 40-50 ms without.
tile pick: the transition form under Type now arrives a pass after the click (PanelRowsArrival after 1): 81.5 -> 44-53 ms.

tried and NOT shipped: (a) letting Effects wait under the fold like other forms: no effect here, it starts inside the 120 pt reach; (b) handing the editor back to Select a turn after Command Return: 61.8 ms, no gain, timeline drew twice.

scope: the 50 ms bar is not reached (after Command Return 64.2/64.6/54.5 ms, tile 53.2/49.9/47.2 ms, three runs). The walk's claims are 100 ms and 65 ms (they fail the old 190-200 and 68-82 ms) and the 50 ms acceptance moved to finishing-a-typed-title-and-picking-a-dissolve-l with the attribution. A 75 ms claim was tried and failed once (80.7 ms, an effect pane arriving), so it would have flapped the rotating check.

walks green with the final build: an-editing-session (3 in a row), 17 effects/appearance walks incl. effects-fit-one-open, measure-row-menu, appearance-and-effects-dropdowns, type-into-an-effects-slider (all four failed until the reach and harness-scroll fixes), 15 transition walks, clip-click-cost, keyframe-anything, undo-redo-cost, arrow-caption-anchor/pill, dock-fits-the-window.
